name: Mitolo Shiraz Savitar 2015
text:
## Mitolo Shiraz Savitar 2015

**The story.** Mitolo is a family-owned McLaren Vale winery founded and led by Frank Mitolo, who set out to draw on his Italian heritage to make wines "of individuality, integrity and utmost quality". In a short time it has come to be recognised as one of the finest producers in McLaren Vale ([Vintus, the US importer](https://lyncdiscovgrinternal.vintus.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/03/Mitolo-Savitar-Shiraz-2015-Tech-Sheet-92-WS.pdf)).

**The wine: Savitar.** "Savitar" is a mythical dragon-like monster. Frank Mitolo and Ben Glaetzer, of the Barossa's Glaetzer winemaking family, named the wine for the impression one small lot in their Willunga vineyard made on them: they were "so blown away" that they decided to bottle it on its own ([Vintus](https://lyncdiscovgrinternal.vintus.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/03/Mitolo-Savitar-Shiraz-2015-Tech-Sheet-92-WS.pdf)). The fruit comes from the Chinese Block of the Lopresti vineyards in the Willunga district, at the southern end of [McLaren Vale](https://www.google.com/maps?q=Willunga,+South+Australia,+Australia&t=k), from an unforgiving, skeletal patch of soil in the block's north-east corner, where the vines struggle and give very low yields. Each parcel spends 15 days on its skins, a little longer than usual, for a tighter structure built for ageing; then 18 months in new, medium-to-light-toast French oak, after which individual barrels are chosen for the final blend. It is 100% [Shiraz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syrah), at 14.5% alcohol ([Vintus](https://lyncdiscovgrinternal.vintus.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/03/Mitolo-Savitar-Shiraz-2015-Tech-Sheet-92-WS.pdf); [Vintus, 2018](https://bnog.vintus.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/05/Mitolo-Savitar-Shiraz-2018-Tech.pdf)).

**From the history books**
- **Named for a McLaren.** McLaren Vale was named after either David McLaren, Colonial Manager of the South Australian Company, or John McLaren, who surveyed the area in 1839. The first settlers grew cereal crops, but John Reynell and Thomas Hardy planted vines in 1838, and the forerunners of today's Seaview and Hardys wineries were running by 1850 ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McLaren_Vale)).
- **Century-old vines.** Some McLaren Vale vines more than 100 years old are still producing ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McLaren_Vale)), and the region is a member of the Great Wine Capitals of the World network.
- **Between the gulf and the hills.** The region runs 30 km down the coast of the [Gulf St Vincent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulf_St_Vincent) to the foothills of the [Mount Lofty Ranges](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mount_Lofty_Ranges), with a [Mediterranean climate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mediterranean_climate) of four clear seasons ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McLaren_Vale)).
- **Penfolds comes south.** Between 1904 and 1912 [Penfolds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penfolds), then the largest winery around Adelaide, bought vineyards in McLaren Vale ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penfolds)).

**The vintage.** [Jancis Robinson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jancis_Robinson)'s [South Australia vintage chart](https://www.jancisrobinson.com/learn/vintages/south-australia) notes bushfires in the Adelaide Hills in 2015 (with some risk of smoke taint there) and an excellent year for Barossa Shiraz; I couldn't read a separate McLaren Vale report.

**What the critics say for 2015.**
- **[Wine & Spirits Magazine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wine_%26_Spirits): 92** (quoted on [Vintus's tech sheet](https://lyncdiscovgrinternal.vintus.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/03/Mitolo-Savitar-Shiraz-2015-Tech-Sheet-92-WS.pdf)). "Tense and understated": from a rocky patch of clay soil less than three miles from Port Willunga, it spent 18 months in new French oak, "but it's the fruit and earth that drives the wine", with wild blueberries, floral black tea, cracked pepper and tar. "An elegant shiraz, brisk and cool in its gentleness. Integrated and restrained, this should age with grace."
- **[CellarTracker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CellarTracker) community: 90.7** (from your CellarTracker list).

**How it's drinking now.** In October 2026 the wine is eleven years old, and your CellarTracker list gives a window of 2024 to 2033. So it is now in its prime: blueberry, pepper and tar softening into savoury, earthy notes. Decant it for an hour, and serve at 16 to 18°C. Drink the 2015 before the 2018.

**Food.** Roast lamb, venison, or a mushroom and beef pie.

**Value and where to buy.** None of the stores on this site lists Mitolo at the moment.

- [Vintus, Mitolo Savitar Shiraz 2015 tech sheet (PDF)](https://lyncdiscovgrinternal.vintus.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/03/Mitolo-Savitar-Shiraz-2015-Tech-Sheet-92-WS.pdf)
